title: OmniStudio Developer Certification: Practice Exam
description: 60-question timed practice exam mirroring the official blueprint domain weights. 105 minutes, pass with 72% or higher.

questions.question: A customer needs integration with a REST system whose availability is uncertain. What is the correct risk treatment?
options: Design fallbacks/error handling (Try/Catch, controlled error responses) and confirm SLAs
questions.explanation: Uncertain external dependencies are managed with error handling and validated assumptions, not hope.

questions.question: A developer deploys OmniStudio components with `sf project deploy`. Which runtime does this imply?
questions.explanation: Source-format CLI deployment is the Standard Runtime pattern; packages use package installs.

questions.question: Which output best reflects 'determining a project's needs'?
options: A solution approach that fits requirements within assumptions, risks, and constraints
A fixed architecture chosen up front
A list of questions with no decisions
A copy of the customer's RFP
questions.explanation: Needs determination converts requirements + constraints into a feasible approach.

questions.question: Which statement about OmniStudio is TRUE?
options: It replaces all Apex and LWC development
It is a declarative toolkit whose components compose across industries and channels
It runs only on Experience Cloud
questions.explanation: OmniStudio is declarative, multi-industry, and channel-agnostic.

questions.question: Which statement about OmniStudio versioning is TRUE?
options: Versioning snapshots component definitions, enabling controlled deployment and rollback
questions.explanation: Versions snapshot definitions for controlled, reversible deployment.

questions.question: How do you move OmniStudio component DEFINITIONS between orgs?
options: Metadata tooling: SF CLI source deploy or VBT package deploy
questions.explanation: Components are metadata. They move with metadata/CLI tooling, not data loaders.

questions.question: A requirement needs field-level security enforced on data shown in a FlexCard. Which data source satisfies the constraint?
questions.explanation: Data Mappers respect FLS; raw SOQL/SOSL data sources do not.

questions.question: Which tools support the end-to-end OmniStudio implementation process?
options: Salesforce CLI (SFCLI), VBT, and Migration Tooling
questions.explanation: The exam guide names SFCLI, VBT, and Migration as implementation tooling.

questions.question: Users still see the old version after a developer saved changes. What is the most likely missing step?
questions.explanation: Save ≠ publish. Components must be published/activated to reach users.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Standard Runtime for OmniStudio components?
options: Components ship inside a managed package
Components are native metadata that ride platform releases and deploy via source format
questions.explanation: Standard Runtime treats components as native metadata; upgrades ride platform releases automatically.

questions.question: A developer needs a new OmniScript 90% identical to an existing one. Fastest supported approach?
options: Clone the existing component and adjust
questions.explanation: Cloning creates a variant from an existing definition quickly and safely.

questions.question: Which mechanism passes data from a host Lightning page INTO a FlexCard?
questions.explanation: Public attributes (and session variables) expose entry points for host context.

questions.question: A FlexCard must render one card per Account from a list. What is required?
options: A data source returning multiple records. The card loops them
questions.explanation: FlexCards iterate over returned records by default. One card per record.

questions.question: Which advanced integration lets you nest one card inside another?
questions.explanation: Child FlexCards nest inside parent cards for composed displays.

questions.question: How should complex multi-source data reach a FlexCard?
options: Via an Integration Procedure in one call
questions.explanation: IPs consolidate orchestration into one server call. The recommended pattern for complex data.

questions.question: What does a FlexCard auto-generate for App Builder / Experience Builder embedding?
questions.explanation: FlexCards generate LWC wrappers for drag-and-drop embedding.

questions.question: During prototyping you embed sample JSON. What must happen before publishing?
options: Replace Custom with a real data source
questions.explanation: Custom JSON is a placeholder; production cards need a real source.

questions.question: When does a Data Mapper data source beat SOQL in a FlexCard?
options: When field-level security or transformation is needed
questions.explanation: Data Mappers respect FLS and transform data; SOQL is simpler but insecure for restricted users.

questions.question: What carries the data when a card action launches an OmniScript?
questions.explanation: Action parameters define what context the launched flow receives.

questions.question: What distinguishes a multi-level FlexCard from a single-level one?
options: Multi-level supports nested/repeated data structures; single-level renders one flat record set
questions.explanation: Multi-level handles nested data via repeaters; single-level is a flat record list.

questions.question: Which is the preferred approach for a one-off emphasis on a single field?
questions.explanation: Inline element styles handle one-off exceptions to the theme.

questions.question: Where should heavy multi-system orchestration live?
options: In an Integration Procedure called by the script
questions.explanation: IPs handle orchestration; OmniScripts stay lean.

questions.question: What makes embedding drag-and-drop on App Builder pages possible?
questions.explanation: OmniScripts generate LWC wrappers for App Builder / Experience Builder.

questions.question: Why test OmniScripts on mobile?
options: Responsive layouts render differently at narrow widths
questions.explanation: Responsive behavior requires per-width verification.

questions.question: An OmniScript must send a confirmation SMS after submission. Which capability?
questions.explanation: Messaging Framework sends SMS/email from OmniScript actions.

questions.question: When can custom LWC elements be used in an OmniScript?
options: When standard elements are insufficient for the UI requirement
questions.explanation: Custom LWCs extend OmniScript UI when standard elements don't suffice.

questions.question: Why must element names be chosen carefully?
options: They become keys in the OmniScript's JSON data structure
questions.explanation: Element names map to JSON keys. They affect formulas, actions, and downstream data.

questions.question: Which tool inspects an OmniScript's data JSON during development?
questions.explanation: Debug mode exposes the JSON and element execution for troubleshooting.

questions.question: What is an OmniScript best described as?
options: A guided experience for completing a business process, built with drag-and-drop elements
questions.explanation: OmniScripts are configurable guided experiences for business processes.

questions.question: What ensures an embedded OmniScript opens pre-populated for the selected record?
options: Passing context (e.g., recordId) into the script
questions.explanation: Context parameters let the script pre-fill from the host page.

questions.question: Users must save a partially completed application and resume later. Which property?
questions.explanation: Save Options enable draft/resume patterns.

questions.question: Which is an OmniScript best practice?
options: Modular child scripts, consistent naming, debug-mode testing
questions.explanation: Best practices favor modularity, naming, and debug testing.

questions.question: When should an IP be chainable?
options: When the process is long-running and exceeds synchronous limits
questions.explanation: Chain long processes; keep short orchestrations synchronous.

questions.question: A long-running process exceeds synchronous transaction limits. What's the right pattern?
options: Chainable IPs splitting work into multiple transactions
questions.explanation: Chainable IPs break long processes into separate transactions.

questions.question: Users see outdated data after reference data changes. What's wrong?
options: Cache TTL/scope misconfiguration or missed invalidation
questions.explanation: Stale data is the classic caching symptom. Tune TTL or invalidate.

questions.question: What is an Integration Procedure?
options: A declarative server-side process executing multiple actions in one call
questions.explanation: IPs orchestrate multiple actions server-side in a single transaction.

questions.question: How can an IP avoid re-fetching the same reference data on every run?
options: Configure caching with a sensible TTL
questions.explanation: Caching stores results for reuse, maximizing performance.

questions.question: An IP must call a REST API using a Named Credential. Which action?
questions.explanation: HTTP Actions make REST callouts; Named Credentials carry auth.

questions.question: Why keep success and error shapes consistent?
options: So callers (FlexCards/OmniScripts) can handle both reliably
questions.explanation: Consistent contracts let UI react to success and failure alike.

questions.question: What should a Catch block do?
options: Log the failure and produce a controlled error response
questions.explanation: Catch blocks log and return predictable errors. Never silent failures.

questions.question: Which action returns data from an IP to its caller?
questions.explanation: The Response Action defines what the IP returns.

questions.question: Which Data Mapper interface is optimized for ONE object plus its related fields?
questions.explanation: Turbo Extract is optimized for single-object + related-field reads.

questions.question: In which Data Mapper interfaces can formulas be used?
questions.explanation: Formulas apply across Transform, Extract, and Load.

questions.question: Which scenario fits Turbo Extract?
options: Pre-filling an OmniScript from one record by Id
Joining five objects with OR filters
questions.explanation: Single-record-centric reads by Id are the Turbo Extract sweet spot.

questions.question: How do you make an Extract reusable across callers?
questions.explanation: Parameterized inputs make mappers reusable artifacts.

questions.question: Which targets can a Data Mapper produce?
options: JSON, XML, Apex class, sObject, PDF, Docusign
questions.explanation: Data Mappers target JSON, XML, Apex classes, sObjects, PDF, Docusign.

questions.question: When is Turbo Extract the better choice over Extract?
options: Reading one object plus related fields with maximum performance
Querying five objects with complex filters
questions.explanation: Turbo Extract is optimized for single-object + related-field reads.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Transform?
options: Reshape/map input data into a required output structure
questions.explanation: Transform maps input to a target structure for APIs, docs, and consumers.

questions.question: How do you produce a list structure (e.g., line items) in the output?
options: Array/repeater mapping over the source array
questions.explanation: Array mapping repeats a structure per source array item.

questions.question: Which interface writes/updates records?
questions.explanation: Load inserts/updates/deletes across objects.

questions.question: You need full name = first + ' ' + last in a Data Mapper output. Which feature?
questions.explanation: Formulas handle concatenation and computed values in mappers.

questions.question: A binding references 'account.Name' but the JSON key is 'Account_Name'. What's wrong?
options: Path typo/mismatch. Paths must match JSON keys exactly
questions.explanation: Path mismatches are the #1 cause of missing values.

questions.question: A FlexCard renders blank. What is the FIRST diagnostic step?
options: Inspect the data JSON from its data source
questions.explanation: Start with the data JSON. Wrong shape/missing fields cause blanks.

questions.question: A deploy fails because a referenced component is missing. What's the issue?
options: Missing metadata / dependency not deployed first
questions.explanation: Deployment failures often trace to missing metadata or dependency order.

questions.question: An action's output is blank and the log shows a malformed payload. What's the problem?
options: Broken JSON. Syntax/escaping issues in the payload
questions.explanation: Malformed payloads appear as missing/blank output. Validate the raw JSON.

questions.question: A user can run OmniScripts but not build them. What's missing?
questions.explanation: Build access requires the admin/builder permission set.

questions.question: A component works in sandbox but fails in production. First check?
options: Version/API compatibility and publish state in production
questions.explanation: Environment differences (versions, publish state) explain sandbox-vs-prod gaps.

questions.question: Users can't see data in a SOQL-backed FlexCard, but admins can. Likely cause?
options: FLS. SOQL data sources don't apply it; use a Data Mapper or grant FLS
questions.explanation: SOQL bypasses FLS; restricted users see blanks.

questions.question: Two output keys have the same name in a mapper. What happens?
questions.explanation: Duplicate keys overwrite values silently.

questions.question: How do you isolate one user's failing interaction in the console?
questions.explanation: Session IDs tie interactions to their logs for isolation.
